traps.why: The alkoxide must attack the RING carbon (SNAr); NaOH does nothing to an aryl halide and there is no OH to alkylate.
There is a reaction: NaOCH₃ / CH₃OH does change 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene.

explanation: The alkoxide adds to the carbon bearing the halide; the ortho/para NO₂ stabilises the negative charge (Meisenheimer complex); the halide then leaves. Addition–elimination, not SN2.
tip: SNAr needs NO₂ ortho or para to the leaving group. Meta: no reaction.
